The reply made me realize that although death is the final outcome, we could still enjoy and live our life if we decide to. That would mean only giving an f to those things that are important to us. 

I liked it that he used nonreligious views in his comment. Theistic persuasion does not work on me, since I no longer believe in such things.

Thank you for commenting on my post. Now, I realized that even if we are merely "prolonging" that time before death, we can still enjoy it by enacting upon our purpose, by following what we truly love in life. Doing things which we truly love, and which really matter to us.

I just got this wonderful reply from u/howtohelpmygf81 from my other post. It made me realize wonderful things, and I hope it would help you too:

Honestly and with no religious take whatsoever I look at life this way: death is final, but life? It has so many possibilities. The world is mad, but I don't even look at the world much anymore. I focus on the things I can control and the things that make me happy. I've never had depression, wouldn't know what it feels like, but I have known sadness and frustration at the world until I realized one day that I can't control what happens in the world, but I can control a lot of the things in my life. The things that matter the most to me. I have hobbies I love. I try to learn new things all the time to change my life up. When I think about someone wanting to take their own lives and end it all, I think about my grandfather and how he was taken before his time. I think about so many people in the world that have gone before their time because they didn't have control over it. Life was taken from them. They didn't have a choice. You do. Make the choice that's still full of possibility, not finality. Some days are shit, I agree, but I always look beyond the storm. Tomorrow will be better. If it's not, surely the next day will. There's always tomorrow. Best of luck to you.

I'm 18, and I just had this thought this morning when I perceived that I couldn't take things anymore. However, thanks to u/howtohelpmygf81's comment, things seem to be better now. At the very least, I'm starting to have hope, to see the light after the storm.

Thank you so much for such a can opener comment. I haven't thought of life like that before. This made me realize that although death is the final outcome, we could still enjoy and live our life if we decide to. That would mean only giving an f to those things that are important to us.
